surface_mechanism_description: The rare earth ions (Ce³+ and Tb³+) partially occupy substitutional sites in the SrS matrix and form RES clusters. The EXAFS analysis indicates that the coordination environment around the RE ions includes both substitutional sites and clusters, with the third coordination sphere returning to the SrS structure, suggesting a local cluster formation.
evidence: The text states: 'The rare earth ions were observed to enter mainly the substitutional sites but at the same time a part of the atoms form RES clusters (RE = rare earth). The presence of both substitutional sites and RES clusters has been observed for the first time in this study for rare earths in II–VI compounds.' Additionally, it mentions: 'The third coordination sphere around the RE ions returns back to the SrS structure.'
